source.title: Towards Better Generalization: BP-SVRG in Training Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Hao Jin; Dachao Lin; Zhi-Hua Zhang

record.tranche_reason: Tests how batch-size choices and learning-rate decay affect held-out performance, using SVRG variants rather than the large-batch training setups in V5.
record.gate_note: The paper varies inner and outer batch sizes and reports CIFAR-10 test accuracy, and compares fixed learning rates with learning-rate decay. Its gradient-norm and generalization-gap plots report separate findings about properties tracking the gap; these do not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness. Results in Tables 3 and 4 compare other optimizers or batch-normalization procedures and are not mapped to a listed version.
record.test_reason: Tables 1–2 test V5 by varying SVRG inner batch size at fixed outer batch and 500 reported epochs. Table 3 also contains a paired VGG11 dropout comparison bearing on V6, overlooked by the record. The study is not an original source for either version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors conclude that mini-batching trades SVRG generalization for scalability, learning-rate decay recovers much of that loss, and their gradient metrics empirically accompany generalization differences. They report BP-SVRG accuracy comparable to SGD(NAG), sometimes better, and generally smaller test loss with fewer dataset traversals. Their gradient-based explanation is heuristic for deep networks.
record.recipe_differences: Compares B-SVRG and BP-SVRG with SGD on CIFAR-10; varies inner and outer batches and applies learning-rate decay. It does not reproduce the cited large-batch protocols.
record.method_sensitivity: Inner batch size, outer batch size, learning-rate decay, optimizer, dataset, and network architecture are varied or compared.

fits_no_version.finding: Across optimization methods, smaller average squared per-sample gradient norms and squared full-gradient norms accompany smaller training–test gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: These gradient metrics empirically track generalization gaps in the tested networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger outer batches generally improve fixed-rate SVRG accuracy; learning-rate decay reduces differences across outer batches.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The accuracy of snapshot-gradient estimation and learning-rate decay affect SVRG generalization.

record.problems: The generalization-error bound assumes P-L conditions, and the authors acknowledge deep networks may not satisfy those assumptions. The gradient-gap relationship is empirical and described as heuristic; the plotted comparisons are smoothed over 5 points. Batch-size experiments in Tables 1 and 2 are limited to AlexNet on CIFAR10.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 reports test accuracies for BP-SVRG, SGD (NAG), and B-SVRG across network-dataset combinations; these optimizer comparisons do not test V4's adaptive-optimizer claim or another listed version. Table 4 compares Modified-SGD and SGD for batch-normalization statistics, not a listed version. Figure 2 and Appendix C show testing-loss comparisons across additional networks and datasets; Table 3 and these additional plots were left out because they do not directly measure the V5 batch-size claim, and Table 3 comparisons fall outside the mapped versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label generalization, and random-label held-out chance performance.
Width variation beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Matched convolutional versus fully connected test-error comparisons and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, limited versus broader tuning, and optimizer adaptations.

Language models, longer training, warmup, normalization or regularization adaptations, and a systematic workload-dependent threshold. The study tests learning-rate scaling and decay, but not scaling with warmup.
Very small training sets, dropout-strength sweeps and underfitting, fully connected classifier comparisons, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, similarly low training-loss controls, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal of memorized versus random training examples and retrained test accuracy.

missing.what: Paired dropout/no-dropout VGG11 accuracies: BP-SVRG 92.98±0.14 versus 92.94±0.16; SGD(NAG) 92.52±0.05 versus 92.60±0.10; B-SVRG 91.96±0.24 versus 92.00±0.23. Although rows_left_out declares Table 3's optimizer comparisons, it overlooks these within-optimizer V6 comparisons.
missing.locator: Table 3, CIFAR10 VGG11 and VGG11 (Dropout); Appendix A.2–A.3

record.verdict_notes: The main V5 comparison is inner batch b at fixed outer batch B. Outer B controls snapshot-gradient estimation and should not be treated as an ordinary SGD update batch. All batch-size settings use learning rates proportional to b, so the observed effects concern that recipe. Algorithm 1 defines an epoch using B examples; equal reported epochs across different B therefore do not guarantee equal dataset exposure. Comparisons at fixed B avoid that exposure confound. Reported uncertainties do not supply significance tests.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD.
Large-batch results on language models; workload-dependent batch thresholds; longer training, learning-rate scaling with warmup, and normalization or regularization adaptations.
Dropout effects and interactions with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbations and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring retrained test accuracy.

rows.subject: VGG11 (Dropout)
rows.operation_detail: Tracked average per-sample gradient norm, average-gradient norm, and training-test loss and accuracy gaps over training for optimization methods.

conditions.value: BPSVRG, BSVRG, SGD and SGD with momentum/Nesterov; no learning-rate decay

rows.measure: gradient norms and training-test loss/accuracy gaps
rows.value: Authors report that methods with smaller values of both gradient metrics have smaller reported gaps; plots show comparisons among the methods.
rows.note: Different measurements from V7's magnitude-aware sharpness; listed under fits_no_version.
rows.check: The empirical finding concerns average squared per-sample gradient norms and squared full-gradient norms. These are not V7's magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation tolerance.

relationships.condition: AlexNet/CIFAR-10, 500 reported epochs, constant learning rates scaled with b; B=50000, 10000 or 5000, b=500 or 1000 versus b=10
